slides.title: LF AI & Data Foundation Welcomes AIRSEAI to Unite Open Source Embodied AI Ecosystem
slides.highlight: The integration of AIRSEAI into the LF AI & Data Foundation supports the development of an open source embodied AI ecosystem, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: RoboColiseum Launches Standardized Simulation Platform for Embodied AI Evaluation
slides.tldr: STANDARDIZED SIMULATION PLATFORM FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: RoboColiseum has launched a standardized simulation platform for evaluating embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: TurnBench: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Turn-Taking Dynamics in Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces TurnBench, a benchmark for end-of-turn and interruption detection across diverse interaction styles, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TurnBench is a multi-domain benchmark for evaluating end-of-turn and interruption detection in spoken dialogue.
card.key_idea: A 30-hour triple-annotated corpus across six interaction styles paired with a standardized evaluation protocol to score heterogeneous turn-taking systems on recall, FPR, and latency.
card.evaluation: 14 systems (rule-based, commercial, and supervised) were tested; VAP performed best, though no system matched human-level turn-transfer timing.
card.limitation: The dataset is limited to English, dyadic conversations recorded in studio conditions, and lacks interruption evaluation for full-duplex models.

slides.title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal Turkish corpus of unscripted dyadic interactions to model turn-taking dynamics, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Introduces Real-TurnTurk, a multimodal Turkish corpus for predicting turn-taking transitions in natural conversations.
card.key_idea: A Genetic Algorithm optimizes interpretable AND-OR decision rules using 28 visual, acoustic, and linguistic features from a 2-second window preceding potential turn changes.
card.evaluation: 5-fold conversation-level cross-validation on 11 dyadic interactions. The GA rule achieved F1=57.0%, modestly outperforming silence thresholds and an always-positive baseline.
card.limitation: Small dataset size (11 conversations) and speaker-level imbalance prevent a fully speaker-disjoint evaluation and claims of statistical significance.

slides.title: Pose-Anchored Optical Flow for Low-Latency Human Action Anticipation in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.highlight: PoseOFF uses pose-anchored optical flow to capture local motion around joints, enabling robots to infer human actions earlier for more responsive interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PoseOFF improves early human action anticipation by anchoring local optical flow features to skeletal joint locations.
card.key_idea: It extracts small optical flow windows around human joints, concatenating these local motion dynamics with skeletal coordinates to create a structured, body-aligned representation for action recognition models.
card.evaluation: Tested on NTU RGB+D 60/120 and UCF101 using InfoGCN++, MS-G3D, and ST-GCN++. Results show improved accuracy and earlier anticipation (AUC) across most classes.
card.limitation: May be less effective under severe occlusion or for actions dominated by large-scale global motion patterns.

slides.authors: Lewis de Zoete Grundy et al.

slides.title: Towards Actionable Surgical Team Dynamics: from Teamwork to Counterfactual Annotations
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal dataset featuring speaker diarization and annotations of group dynamics and interaction processes, supporting HyECHO's focus on social perception and team state modeling.

card.one_liner: Introduces an extended multimodal surgical dataset with multi-level teamwork and counterfactual annotations to analyze team dynamics.
card.key_idea: Enriches the MM-OR dataset with speaker diarization, bilingual transcripts, and a hierarchical annotation framework (team, interaction, individual levels) plus counterfactual breakdown triggers.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via expert human annotations across multiple frameworks (OTAS, HMT, NOTSS, BFTQ, SYMLOG, GLIS) on 169 video samples.
card.limitation: Moderate class imbalance in ratings, as recorded surgical teams generally demonstrated acceptable performance, making extreme ratings rare.

slides.authors: Vincenzo Marco De Luca et al.

slides.title: Generative Action-Chunk Sampling for Adaptive Stiffness Control in Physical Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE STIFFNESS VIA GENERATIVE ACTION SAMPLING
slides.highlight: This research introduces a framework that uses variation in sampled action chunks to balance assistance and compliance, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Adaptive robot stiffness control using variation among sampled action chunks to balance assistance and compliance during pHRI.
card.key_idea: A CVAE-based policy samples multiple action chunks from an observation-conditioned prior; high variance among samples triggers lower stiffness for human guidance.
card.evaluation: Real-world collaborative transport task (4 directions); achieved 0.95 success rate vs. 0.83 (fixed-stiffness) and 0.69 (deterministic FACTR).
card.limitation: Action-deviation signal is a proxy for uncertainty, not a calibrated probability of human intention or epistemic uncertainty.

slides.title: Simulating Cognitive Smart Freight Corridors with Agent-Based Models and Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODELING FOR COGNITIVE FREIGHT CORRIDORS
slides.highlight: This research utilizes agent-based modeling and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive behaviors in smart freight corridors, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: An ABM framework using RL and MARL to optimize platoon formation and charging in smart freight corridors.
card.key_idea: A three-layer architecture (physical, cyber, decision) integrating a DQN corridor controller for lane/platoon management and MARL agents for distributed charging station pricing and priority coordination.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via three scenarios (Baseline, Assisted, Cognitive) using throughput, congestion, and energy metrics. Results show Cognitive scenario improves throughput by 27% and reduces congestion by 63.9%.
card.limitation: The model uses a unidirectional network and lacks comparisons with established optimization benchmarks or extensive statistical testing.

slides.title: Dual-Scale State-Space Modeling with Speaker-Wise Dynamic CRF for Speech Emotion Recognition in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work proposes DSSM-CRF to model emotion evolution and cross-speaker influence in conversations, contributing to HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: DSSM-CRF improves conversational speech emotion recognition by separating cross-speaker context from within-speaker emotion evolution.
card.key_idea: Dual-scale bidirectional state-space models encode frame and dialogue context, while a speaker-wise dynamic CRF decodes independent emotion chains using global priors and pair-conditioned transition residuals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP and MELD against multiple baselines. Results (e.g., 75.81% UA on IEMOCAP) are supported by component ablations and backbone robustness tests.
card.limitation: Abrupt within-speaker emotion changes (shifts) remain significantly harder to predict than emotional persistence (inertia).
